seal.statement: The production-owner composition hosted by the deterministic simulator reproduces all four live failure properties on the sealed strict substrate: seed watchdog gap fraction at least 50 percent with every joiner under 5 percent; incomplete-lease observations naming all five nodes with escalating backoff; priority spread gap non-decreasing with zero operations in flight; and admission ending in control_plane_pressure. Each missing property is closed by identifying the first missing causal arrow between the calibrated live formation and the simulator and hosting the real production boundary that supplies it - never by synthetic frequency, injected CPU, multiplied invocation counts or tuned coefficients.

text: Frontier 1 is C1 and the owner-rate audit selects reality C. Across 79 seed watchdog callbacks the maximum lateness is 99 ms and none exceeds the 1000 ms threshold, so zero observed gaps is the correct answer for the workload the simulator currently generates: the watchdog is not at fault and the seed is only 5.3 percent busy, 1066 charged ms in a 20,026 ms window. The audit, per second of window on the seed, against the frozen live calibration: raft_protocol 22,560 live against 319.5 sim, a ratio of 0.014; membership_publication 2,727 against 0.9, a ratio of 0.0003; rebalancer 2,237 against 389, a ratio of 0.174; readiness 2.2 against 2.8, the only owner at its live rate and the one whose live rate is lowest. bootstrap, transport, admin and raft_apply never run. So it is NOT primarily the absent 14.9 percent: the three hosted dominant owners, 73.2 percent of the live window, are short by 70x, 3000x and 5.7x. That rules out candidate A - hosting the missing owners cannot by itself saturate the seed - and leaves the first missing arrows inside the hosted owners' triggers, with candidate B still open, since bootstrap and raft_apply may drive protocol and publication work. Frontiers 3 and 4 are deliberately not instrumented yet: predicates 2 and 4 are downstream of seed saturation, and tracing them now would measure a consequence.

Q1a answers the question before Q1b can be asked: the simulator does not host the production population, and its placement is structurally inverted. Measured, not derived from rows - 120 distinct directed peer edges with multiplicity 6 per node pair across node-0 to node-4, so 6 groups times 5 instances is 30 Raft objects, one per node per group. formation-sim-raft-cohort.js constructs new LifeRaft directly: the harness chooses why each group exists (one per PRIORITY_CONTROL_PLANE_TABLE_IDS entry, which are TABLE ids and not partition ids), the replica identities, their execution nodes, the election start via rafts.get(seedId).promote(), and peer addition on membership change. Under the design's own rule those are owner decisions, and all six are currently the harness's. Against the cold-formation contract of 45 critical partitions at RF 3 - 45 verified in this tree - 135 replicas concentrated on the seed: instances 135 against 30, directed peer edges 270 against 120, leader peer edges 90 against 24. Normalised, seg/s per raft instance is 167.11 live against 10.65 sim, per directed peer edge 83.55 against 2.66, per leader peer edge 250.66 against 13.31. Population explains about 4x of the raw 70x, leaving a 15 to 20x opportunity-normalised deficit that is NOT yet evidence of a missing protocol trigger because the population it is normalised against is wrong. Classification is P0 and P1 together, so Q1b is not started. Note also that the frozen calibration report carries owner costs and a verdict but no population census, so additional live Raft groups are unenumerated - a gap in the frozen evidence rather than a claim that none existed.
